question.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2-x-y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}-y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|1}=\frac{1}{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(2-x-y)}{(\frac{3}{2}-y)} \\  & =\frac{4-2x-2y}{3-2y},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{4-2x-2\cdot 1}{3-2\cdot 1}=\frac{4-2x-2}{3-2}=2-2x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(2-2x)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{4-3}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1]-{\mu }_{X|1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
